about: The expert council (queue expert-council): what the best professionals would make every household do, as small systems anyone can run. Item 1: single points of failure (risk officers, supply-chain and reliability engineers) and paper hygiene (lawyers). Paraphrased from common professional practice, verified on the date shown; rules differ by bank, insurer and state, so each item says where to confirm. Not legal or financial advice.

spof.lens: Risk officer: one income with no cover is the household's largest single point of failure.
spof.title: If the main earner's income stopped, would the family be covered?
fix: Buy pure term life cover; a common planning rule is about 10 to 15 times the yearly income, plus the loans outstanding.
Name the spouse or a parent as nominee on the policy.
Keep the emergency fund at six months of essential costs.
spof.confirm: Compare term plans on the insurers' own sites or IRDAI-registered aggregators

spof.lens: Reliability engineer: knowledge held by one person is a single point of failure.
spof.title: If you were unreachable tomorrow, could your family find the money and the papers?
fix: Write one family emergency file: banks, investments, insurance, loans, the doctor, where the papers are, who to call (the template below).
Store it encrypted and give one trusted person access; a password manager's emergency-access feature does this well.
Review it every six months.

template.title: Family emergency file
template.text: Banks and accounts (bank, branch, account type, nominee): ... | Investments (where held, how to reach the statement): ... | Insurance (insurer, policy no., nominee, agent's number): ... | Loans (lender, EMI date): ... | Property papers (where kept): ... | Doctor and medicines: ... | Who to call first: ... | Where the will is: ...

spof.lens: Lawyer: an account with no nominee can take the family months of paperwork to reach.
spof.title: Does every account, deposit, demat, fund, EPF and policy have a nominee?
fix: List every account and investment from your bank apps and the CAS statement.
Add or update the nominee in each app or branch; many banks now allow more than one nominee with a share each.
Keep a screenshot of each confirmation in the emergency file.
spof.confirm: Each bank, depository participant, fund house and the EPFO member portal

spof.lens: Supply-chain engineer: one supplier is one point of failure.
spof.title: If one bank account were frozen or hacked, could you still pay for a month?
fix: Keep a second bank account with one month of essential costs.
Make the household account joint (either or survivor) where it fits.
Keep a small cash reserve at home for a few days.

spof.lens: Security engineer: every one-time password on one phone is a single point of failure.
spof.title: If your phone were lost today, could you still get into your bank and email?
fix: Save the backup codes for email and the password manager, printed and kept with the papers.
Register a second number or device where the bank allows it.
Know the steps to block the SIM and the UPI apps: the bank's and the telco's helpline numbers in the emergency file.
spof.confirm: Your email provider, bank and telco

spof.lens: Actuary: health cover tied to a job ends with the job, when you may need it most.
spof.title: Is there health cover that stays if the job ends?
fix: Buy a personal family floater, or a super top-up over the group policy (usually much cheaper).
Buy it while healthy: waiting periods start from the day it begins.
Add parents' cover separately (and Ayushman for those over 70).

spof.lens: Lawyer: without a will, the law decides who inherits, and families wait.
spof.title: Is there a will?
fix: Write a simple will: who gets what, an executor, a guardian for minor children.
Sign it before two witnesses who are not beneficiaries; registering it is optional but helps.
Tell the executor where it is; note it in the emergency file. Review after any big life event.
spof.confirm: A lawyer for anything beyond a simple estate

spof.lens: Doctor: in an emergency, the family decides faster when your wishes are written down.
spof.title: Does your family know your medical wishes, and who decides if you cannot?
fix: Write down your wishes and name one person to decide for you (India recognises advance medical directives).
Keep a medical card: blood group, allergies, medicines, conditions, doctor's number, in the wallet and the phone's emergency info.
Share it with the person you named.

spof.lens: Lawyer and records manager: a paper you cannot find is a paper you do not have.
spof.title: Are the important papers in one place, with a safe digital copy?
fix: One folder: identity, property, insurance, investments, loans, education, vehicle.
Scan each into an encrypted folder; use DigiLocker for the government documents it issues.
Note in the emergency file where both are.
